title: Relative isomorphism graph classifications and natural representing bijections
statement: Let $S,X,Y$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme] with maps $x:X\to S$, $y:Y\to S$. For $T\to S$, write $X_T=T\times_S X$, $Y_T=T\times_S Y$ [def-pc-fibre-product] and $F(T)=\operatorname{Isom}_T(X_T,Y_T)$. Define restriction along $h:T\prime\to T$ by commutation of the canonical pullback squares for both the forward map and its inverse. Define $\Gamma_e=(1,e):X_T\to X_T\times_T Y_T$. A bijection $E:A\simeq F(T)$ is a graph classification if every $\Gamma_{E(a)}$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and every closed immersion $j:D\to X_T\times_TY_T$ with projection isomorphisms $p:D\simeq X_T$, $q:D\simeq Y_T$ gives a unique $a$ with $E(a)=q p^{-1}$ and the same closed subscheme as $\Gamma_{E(a)}$ (equality of defining ideals). A graph representation by $J/S$ is such a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_S(T,J)\simeq F(T)$ for every $T/S$, natural under these canonical restrictions. The Zariski sheaf condition means that on every set-indexed open-immersion cover [def-weil-open-immersion] of every $T$, compatible isomorphisms glue uniquely, with both the forward and inverse restriction squares. Compatibility can equivalently be tested on every pair of chart maps from the same test scheme whose composites to $T$ agree. For $b:B\to S$ and $T/B$, define the canonical reassociation $T\times_B(X\times_SB)\simeq T\times_SX$ by symmetry and pullback pasting; define the map between the graph ambient products by these reassociations and the identity on $T$.
